| The question | Where the study answers it | What you fill in |
|:--|:--|:--|
| What did this study collect? | The cylinders and page-shaped elements the flow writes into | `Dataset`, `Table`, `Timeseries`, `EventMarker` |
| What shape is it? | The element you chose, and a `Schema` attached to it | `format`, `schema`, `body` |
| Which standard does it follow? | The badge on the cylinder | `format`, then `bdmDataLevel` or `bidsDataType` |
| Where does it live? | The element itself; a dataset may also name a listing and a store | `uri`, `catalog`, `storage` |
| What does this step read and write? | The dashed lines around the step, and their direction | nothing --- it is read off the drawing |
| Which argument does this value arrive as? | The label on the dashed line | `slot = selection` |
| What does the run carry that is never drawn? | The study's own declared values | `bpmn:Property` |

## What did this study collect?

![A preprocessing pipeline: one dataset read in at the left, another written out at the right.](../assets/img/examples/lablink_demo2.studyflow.png){#fig-data-flow fig-alt="A left-to-right pipeline. A cylinder labelled Raw BIDS data sits below the first step, Read BIDS dataset, joined to it by a dashed arrow pointing up into the step. The flow continues through Drop QC failures, a fan-out into fMRIPrep and EEGPrep, then Collect features, Fit model, Generate figures, and Render manuscript table, from which a dashed arrow points down into a cylinder labelled Manuscript artifacts."}

| If the value is | Draw |
|:--|:--|
| A collection published under a data standard | `Dataset` |
| A description of how something is laid out, in CSVW, LinkML, or JSON Schema | `Schema` |
| Rows and columns, with that structure committed to | `Table` |
| A recording sampled continuously over time | `Timeseries` |
| Time-stamped occurrences inside a recording | `EventMarker` |
| A named group of settings | `Parameters` |
| A public listing that datasets are published in | `DataCatalog` |
| Anything else passing between steps | `bpmn:DataObjectReference` |
| Bytes that persist somewhere, with no further claim about them | `bpmn:DataStoreReference` |

## What shape is it?

Three elements commit to a structure a plain data object leaves open.

| Element | What it is | What it carries |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `Table` | rows and columns: a trial table, a participant list | `format` --- `csv` by default, or `tsv`, `parquet`, `arrow`, `jsonl` --- and `rowCount` |
| `Timeseries` | a continuous recording: EEG, EMG, eye tracking, an accelerometer stream | `samplingRate` in Hz, `channelCount`, `units`, `recordingDuration` in seconds, and a `format` such as `edf`, `bdf`, `fif`, `set`, `parquet`, `zarr` |
| `EventMarker` | the sparse counterpart: trial markers, stimulus onsets, button presses | `eventType`, `eventOnset`, `eventOffset`, `eventCount` |

::: {.callout-important}
## Two clocks

`eventOnset` and `eventOffset` are seconds from the start of a recording; `onset` and `duration` on an activity are the study's schedule, in visits and days.
:::

### What do the columns mean?

A `Schema` says what is *in* the data, one level down from what kind of thing it is.

| Field | What goes in it |
|:--|:--|
| `format` | `csvw`, `linkml`, `jsonschema` |
| `body` | the schema itself, or a path or URL to it |
| `schema`, on a `Dataset` or a `Table` | points at the `Schema` element |

A CSVW or LinkML column list is edited as a table of columns: name, datatype, description, and whether it is required. Any other format is edited as plain text.

## Which standard does it follow?

A `Dataset` is a *logical* collection: one thing the study reads or produces, possibly many files and several modalities.

| `format` | Standard | Then asks for |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `bdm` | [Behaverse Data Model](https://behaverse.org/data-model/) | `bdmDataLevel`: events, trials, or models |
| `bids` | [Brain Imaging Data Structure](https://bids.neuroimaging.io/) | `bidsDataType`: anat, beh, eeg, func, meg, and the rest |
| `psych-ds` | [Psych-DS](https://psych-ds.github.io/) | --- |
| `kedro` | [Kedro datasets](https://docs.kedro.org/projects/kedro-datasets/) | --- |

## Where does it live?

| Field | On | What it says |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `uri` | every data element | Unset, the value only passes from step to step in memory. Set, it is loaded and saved there, in the declared `format` or the one the file extension implies. It is the only storage field the notation has. |
| `catalog` | a `Dataset` | The `DataCatalog` it is published in --- `openneuro`, `behaverse`. You name one rather than drawing one. |
| `storage` | a `Dataset` | The `bpmn:DataStoreReference` where the bytes physically live. |

## What does this step read and write?

Connect a data element to a step and it is an input. Connect the step to a data element and it is an output. The inspector lists these as that step's *Inputs* and *Outputs*, read off the drawing rather than typed in.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Use a data connector, not the plain artifact connector

`bpmn:Association` draws the same dashed line but carries no meaning, so a step joined that way records no data. The line looks right and does nothing.
:::

### Which argument does this value arrive as?

Write it on the connector itself, as `slot = selection`. The **slot** names where the value goes; the **selection** names which value arrives.

A selection can only pick a value out and route it. Anything that computes has to be a step of its own.

```yaml
Fit:
  type: bpmn:ServiceTask
  implementation: python://sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline.fit
  dataInputAssociations:
    Association_Estimator_Fit:
      transformation: self        # the receiver, bound first and by position
      sourceRef: [Estimator]
    Association_Features_Fit:
      transformation: X = folds['train']
      sourceRef: [Folds]
  dataOutputAssociations:
    Association_Fit_Model:
      targetRef: Model            # the element you drew is the slot
```

Two slots are positions rather than names. `self` is the receiver of an unbound method and is bound first. `*` appends its value in the order written. On an *output* association there is no slot to name: the element you drew is itself the slot.

## What does the run carry that is never drawn?

| When the value is | Say it as | Where it lives |
|:--|:--|:--|
| a thing the study reads or produces --- a dataset, a table, a fitted model, a figure | a data element | drawn, with dashed edges, a place in the auto-layout, and a `uri` if it should outlive the run |
| run state a branch condition reads by name --- the arm a participant was assigned, a running accuracy | a `bpmn:Property`, typed `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, or any other type name you enter | declared on a process or sub-process, in the inspector's *Execution* tab; never drawn |
| a literal the call still needs --- `cv: 5`, `n_components: 16` --- fixed before the run | `additionalArguments` | on the step |
| settings you want visible on the canvas and wired into the steps that read them | a `Parameters` element | drawn |

Properties follow ordinary scoping rules: a name resolves outward through the containers around it, and an inner declaration of the same name hides an outer one.

::: {.callout-note}
Two connections draw no line: one to a property, and one reaching out of a sub-process into the study around it. Both are still listed in the inspector.
:::
